name: Thoroughbred — longer-leg study
prompt: Make this Thoroughbred’s legs 5% longer while keeping it a living horse. Rebuild its geometry, joints and walking reach together; preserve its coat seed and original reference dossier.

sources.title: Purdue Extension: Hoof Anatomy, Care and Management in Livestock
sources.note: External reference only; no illustration is redistributed. Cattle have paired principal hoof digits; horses have one continuous hoof.

sources.title: University of Minnesota: Gait glossary
sources.note: Walk timing and contact terminology. Procedural motion is a simplified interpretation, not motion capture.

sources.title: Oklahoma State University: Thoroughbred Horses
sources.note: Breed conformation and reference photographs; historical text is used only for morphology, not current breed statistics. Photographs are not redistributed.

sources.title: University of Minnesota Extension: Conformation of the horse
sources.note: External shape, head/neck relationship and limb landmarks. These qualitative guidelines do not define validated ranges for the model parameters.

sources.title: University of Minnesota Extension: Caring for the overweight horse
sources.note: Equine 1-to-9 condition score context; target score remains subject to visual review.

sources.title: UC Davis Veterinary Genetics Laboratory: Agouti (Bay/Black)
sources.note: Bay coloration and distribution of dark pigment. The generated coat is an appearance choice, not a claim of a tested genotype.

sources.title: Crook et al. (2010): The effect of treadmill speed and gradient on equine hindlimb muscle activity
sources.note: Primary-study abstract: six horses on a treadmill at walk speeds of 1.4-1.6 m/s and differing gradients. Context only; it does not establish the model stride length, stance fraction or hoof pitch, nor a Thoroughbred breed range. No article assets are bundled.

evidence.notes: An adult Thoroughbred gelding is the selected subject. This is an original generic specimen, not a named registered horse.
Long head and neck, defined withers, deep chest, hindquarter muscles and different front/hind joint layouts guide the original surface.
Body proportions follow qualitative reference relationships. The configurable range is an engineering envelope, not population measurement data.
Each foot has one continuous hoof capsule. The model is unshod and retains hoof/pastern distinction.
Brown body with dark mane, tail and lower limb points; no claim of genetic testing. Exact color and highlights are original material choices.

Four-beat walking is interpreted from the glossary with equine treadmill study context. The baseline 1.5 m full stride, 1.2 m/s speed, .65 front/hind stance fractions, approximately 8.9-degree peak absolute swing hoof pitch, and joint/body trajectories are authored settings, not measurements established by the cited abstract or validated Thoroughbred limits. Review the complete cycle and actual hoof-shell contact. The 5% longer-leg edit rescales stride and cycle duration through the implementation; it is not evidence for how a real longer-legged horse moves.
Target moderate 5/9 equine condition; inspect muscle and rib contours rather than treating the number as a computed measurement.

notes: Original procedural anatomy study; anatomical and visual approval pending.
This profile represents an adult gelding and does not implement reproductive anatomy.
Head tracking and jaw motion are deliberately bounded demonstrations, not a complete equine behavior repertoire.
No trot, canter, gallop, jumping or anatomical internal organs are supported.
Mane and tail use portable geometry; hair strands are an approximation.
Reference images are linked, not bundled. Original geometry/material generation is covered by the repository license.

Derived from thoroughbred; seed 314159 and reference dossier preserved. Edits: proportions.legLength=1.05. Geometry, rig, attachments, and motion must be regenerated together; visual review is pending.
Gait distances, stance fractions and hoof flexion are original authored animation controls informed by linked study context. Numeric contact checks do not establish anatomical or visual approval.
